content:
Shapes, patterns and symmetry are the most visual part of the Class 1 Olympiad — and the part where a clear picture in the child's head beats memorising. This guide sets out what is tested, the shape facts to know cold, the common mix-ups, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 1 Shapes and Patterns Olympiad tests

  • Naming 2-D shapes (circle, square, rectangle, triangle, oval) and counting sides and corners
  • Naming 3-D shapes (cube, cuboid, sphere, cylinder, cone) and their faces
  • Continuing a repeating pattern
  • Spotting a line of symmetry

Key facts your child should know

  • A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners; a square has 4 equal sides; a circle has no corners.
  • A cube has 6 faces, 8 corners and 12 edges; a cuboid is the same but like a brick.
  • A cylinder has 2 flat faces and 1 curved; a sphere (a ball) has no flat face.
  • A shape has a line of symmetry when a fold makes two matching halves.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Mixing up corners and sides when counting.
  • Calling every box a cube — a cube has all equal sides, a cuboid does not.
  • Continuing a pattern by colour when the rule is really about shape (or the other way round).

quiz.title: IMO Class 1 Shapes and Patterns Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Class 1 Maths: Shapes and Patterns

questions.q: Which of these shapes has NO corners at all?
questions.explanation: A circle is one smooth curve with no corners. The other three all have corners.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a flat (2D) shape?
questions.explanation: A cube is a solid (3D) shape you can hold; the others are flat shapes you draw.

questions.q: How many corners does a oval have?
questions.explanation: An oval is one smooth egg-like curve, so it has no corners.

questions.q: A pattern repeats like this: red, blue, red, blue, ... What is the 10th colour?
questions.explanation: The block of 2 repeats. The 10th colour matches the 2nd one in the block, so it is blue.

questions.q: Which of these letters looks the same when you fold it down the middle?
questions.explanation: Fold A down its middle and the two halves match exactly.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT look the same on both of its sides?
questions.explanation: A shoe curves for one foot, so its two sides are different. The others have matching halves.
Each number is 2 more than the one before it, so the blank is 6.

questions.q: A door is shaped most like a ___.
questions.explanation: A door is longer than it is wide, with 4 corners — a rectangle.

questions.q: Look at the letter pattern: A B B A B B. Which letter comes next?
questions.explanation: The letters repeat in the block "A B B". After 6 letters the pattern needs A next.

questions.q: A brick used for building a wall has which solid shape?
questions.explanation: A brick is box-shaped but longer than it is tall, so it is a cuboid.

faq.q: How many faces does a cube have?
faq.a: Six. All six faces of a cube are equal squares, and it also has 8 corners and 12 edges.

faq.q: What is a line of symmetry?
faq.a: A line that splits a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded along it.
